chapter: Jump for Joy, records and royalties
title: Hammond's allowance and partying at New York after-hours spots
summary: Hammond's money was on top of club pay; Turner partied and sang at after-hours joints.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You said that you were working for Barney Josephson but you said that John Hammond used to pay you. Is that the way it was? Barney Josephson didn't pay you. It was John Hammond that gave you your money every week?
John Hammond just give that to me.
Oh. Oh, that was in addition to what you made at the club?

He just give me money so's I'd have a good time. He want me stay in New York. He had plans for me. I'se get homesick... lonesome. I don't like New York. He say, 'You stick around. You go out and have a good time.'
Well, I'd go...I went to every joint I know. People thought I was rich, I guess, an' I was buyin' drinks, havin' a party. I had a good time.
We had so much fun...I didn't know when to go home. I stay out all night long. When you get through with your regular job, you go to the after-hours joint.
Did you sing in any of the after-hours joints, or were you just partying?
You just go in there and sing and have a good time...just jammin'.
